# Engineering Knowledge Base Foundation

## Mission

Build a reusable body of software engineering knowledge that helps humans and AI produce better engineering decisions, artifacts, and software.

## Core Belief

AI-assisted engineering is only reliable when AI has access to explicit engineering knowledge.

The goal is not to trust model memory.

The goal is to provide a stable knowledge base that defines engineering quality.

## EKB Responsibilities

EKB should explain:

- what good requirements look like
- what good architecture looks like
- what good design looks like
- what good testing looks like
- what good security thinking looks like
- what good accessibility thinking looks like
- what good engineering documentation looks like

## EKB Must Be

- reusable
- technology-neutral where possible
- practical
- human-readable
- AI-readable
- example-driven
- version-controlled

## EKB Must Avoid

- project-specific decisions
- tool-specific instructions unless clearly marked
- vague advice without criteria
- duplicating ECF process rules
- pretending best practices are universal without context

## Relationship to ECF

EKB provides engineering knowledge.

ECF uses that knowledge to define:

- standards
- transformations
- artifact quality criteria
- reviews
- quality gates

## Guiding Statement

Good engineering requires more than process.

It requires shared knowledge of what quality means.
